title: Session-aware metering sharder and attribution bridge for late-arrival tokens
creator: Ava Chen
description:
Problem: We observe repeated late-arrival token batches from edge proxies that complicate per-session attribution and cause double-counting or lost credits when consumers retry across routes. Current ledger joiner assumes near-real-time ordering and single-source ingestion, leading to opaque adjustments in downstream billing jobs.

Goal: Implement a session-aware sharder + attribution bridge that groups token events by stable session fingerprint, applies idempotent deduplication, and emits reconciled attribution records into the billing canonical topic. This bridge should tolerate out-of-order delivery, support eventual consistency windows, and provide deterministic tombstones for corrected events so downstream jobs (ledger compactor, invoice builder) can consume without special-casing late arrivals.
spec:
High-level design:
1) Session Fingerprinting: Use existing session_key heuristic (tenant_id + client_session_token + route_hash) and fall back to probabilistic fingerprint (first-10-chars of request_id + truncated KV-hash) for older payloads.
2) Windowing: Maintain a sliding reconciliation window configurable per-tenant (default 90s, max 15m). Events outside the reconciliation window are marked as 'late' and go through a slow-path.
3) Sharder: Map session fingerprints to 64 Kafka partitions using jump-consistent-hash so events for the same session collocate.
4) Dedup & Conflict Resolution: Apply last-write-wins with tie-breaker on ingest_origin and sequence_number; record resolved event id and tombstone when supplanting previous attribution.
5) Output Schema: Emit canonical_attribution records to topic console.billing.canonical.v2 with fields (session_fingerprint, attribution_key, tokens_consumed, window_id, resolved_at, source_tags, tombstone_flag).
6) Backpressure & Throttling: Enforce per-tenant inflight limit; surface soft-fail metric to Console when limits breached.
7) Compatibility: Provide a compatibility shim that can produce the older 'legacy_attribution' envelope for a 30-day grace period to avoid consumer breakage.
implementation_notes:
- Implement as a Flink job in the analytics cluster (aligns with existing streaming infra).
- Use RocksDB keyed state per session_fingerprint to keep minimal metadata (last_seen_ts, last_event_id, accumulated_tokens, window_id). TTL set to 24h for safety.
- Use protobuf schema registry (proto v3) for canonical_attribution; coordinate with schema team for version bump.
- Add a feature flag to switch routing of the canonical topic from the old aggregator to the new bridge for a single tenant for canary.
- Estimate: ~6 sprint days to implement + 2 days for QA and rollout orchestration.
- Implementation owner: Marcus (code), Priya Nair (spec review), SRE: Jamal Ortiz (deploy/alerts).
acceptance_criteria:
- The bridge hashes events to the same partition for identical session_fingerprints (unit test).
- Deduplication eliminates producer-duplicate records in end-to-end integration tests (simulate producer retry).
- Late-arrival events within 15m window are merged into existing canonical_attribution messages and emit a tombstone for any replaced record.
- Downstream billing job (ledger compactor) consumes canonical_attribution.v2 and produces identical invoice lines for canary tenant as legacy pipeline (bitwise match on sample subset).
- Metrics: per-tenant duplicate-rate decreases by >= 90% for test traffic; added observability dashboards show reconciliation latency P95 < 120s for default window.
- Rollout: able to enable for single tenant via feature flag and rollback without data divergence.
migration_plan:
Phase 1 (canary): Deploy job in read-only mode that writes reconciliation metrics and a shadow canonical topic; enable for a single low-volume tenant (teammate: Solutions Eng to coordinate).
Phase 2 (validation): Enable write-mode for canary tenant; compare ledger outputs for 24h, run checksum tests.
Phase 3 (gradual ramp): Flip feature flags for increasing tenant cohorts by traffic percentage, monitor duplication and reconciliation dashboards.
Phase 4 (compatibility wind-down): After 30 days of parity, notify consumers and start producing only canonical_attribution.v2; deprecate legacy envelope after 60 days.
testing_plan:
- Unit tests: partition mapping, fingerprint collision heuristics, dedup logic, tombstone emission.
- Integration tests: end-to-end with a local Kafka+Flink test harness; simulate out-of-order, duplicate, and late events.
- Load test: run synthetic traffic at 5x expected peak for a tenant, assert state store memory and checkpoint frequency remain acceptable.
- Chaos test: kill job mid-window, restart, ensure idempotent recovery and consistent tombstone semantics.
- Customer-facing regression: run ledger compactor comparison for two weeks on canary tenant.
observability:
- Metrics: reconciliation_window_latency_ms (p50/p95/p99), per_tenant_duplicate_rate, tombstone_emitted_count, partition_skew_ratio, state_store_size_bytes, late_event_count.
- Logs: structured logs with session_fingerprint, window_id, resolved_event_id, conflict_reason.
- Dashboards: Console -> Analytics -> Attribution -> 'Session Reconciliation' (new) with tenant filter and alert thresholds: duplicate_rate > 1% for 30m (P1), reconciliation_latency_p95 > 3m (P2).
- Tracing: add trace spans for fingerprinting -> dedup -> emit with linkable trace_id from incoming request if present.
risks:
- Schema drift: Consumers may not adopt canonical_attribution.v2 quickly, requiring extended compatibility shim.
- State growth: High-cardinality session keys for bots or abuse could blow RocksDB memory; mitigation: adaptive cardinality caps and sample eviction.
- Ordering assumptions: Some upstream proxies may rewrite session tokens; fingerprint heuristics must be robust to avoid divergent attribution.
- Rollback complexity: Once tombstones are emitted, reversing reconciliation deterministically is tricky; require audit logs and dry-run mode.
